summary: Surveyed all 25 listed files (sizes, per-file declaration counts via grep for theorem/lemma/def/structure/inductive/instance/abbrev/class, sorry counts). 22 files carry Lean declarations and proofs formalizing Datalog syntax, grounding, substitution, semantics, unification, model checking, proof-tree and graph (walk, DFS, cycle) validation, and supporting list/tree/hashset lemmas. The three aggregators (CertifyingDatalog.lean, Datalog.lean, GraphValidation.lean) contain the Lean `module` command and `public import` lines, which take them outside the pure-import class under FILTER-007, and they are the module-path entry points. lakefile.lean is the package's Lean build declaration and records the mathlib dependency; it is small and gives provenance. No file meets the FILTER-004 bar for hard exclusion; disposition is retain with no rules.

summary: Inspected all 21 files in the CertifyingDatalog Lean repository. Every file contains formal mathematical content: definitions (structures, inductive types, abbreviations), lemmas/theorems with proofs, typeclass instances, and algorithms for Datalog syntax, grounding, substitution, semantics, unification, model checking, graph/tree validation, and supporting data structure lemmas. No file is a pure import aggregator (all contain executable/formal commands beyond imports per FILTER-007). No file meets FILTER-004 hard-exclusion criteria — none are devoid of formal mathematical declarations/proofs, and none have content exactly duplicated elsewhere. The lakefile.lean provides build provenance (mathlib v4.34.1 dependency). Main.lean contains the CLI entry point with verification theorems. All files retain searchable formal mathematics.
